_Oct 12 – Oct 26, 2026_

## K-12 Curriculum & Instruction

Recent news coverage in Chicago K-12 public education primarily focused on developments related to the upcoming school board elections and labor relations, rather than K-12 curriculum and instruction. Articles highlighted the ongoing school board election campaigns, including fact-checking campaign materials and discussing public expectations for an elected board. There was also reporting on a candidate for Board President addressing a closed investigation.

Additionally, the Chicago Board of Education approved a new union contract for lunchroom workers, which includes wage increases. Discussions also touched on the potential implications of an elected school board on future property tax decisions for the district. No direct developments or emerging trends concerning K-12 curriculum or instructional practices were reported in the provided articles.

## Students & School Life

Recent reports indicate Chicago Public Schools (CPS) has seen an increase in high school graduation and college enrollment rates for the Class of 2026, with the graduation rate reaching 83.4 percent. While these figures are being celebrated, some reports also highlight that many students continue to face challenges in completing their post-secondary education. Concurrently, issues affecting student well-being and learning environments have emerged. CPS approved a significant settlement for a family whose child experienced years of racist bullying, underscoring concerns about student safety and equity. Separately, parents have raised claims that some special education students are being taught in hallways, pointing to potential resource and space challenges for this student population.

In related developments, the upcoming election for the Chicago school board president has drawn attention to candidates' plans for student achievement and budget management. Candidates have been questioned on how they intend to boost student outcomes and address the needs of the school community. On the operational front, the Chicago Board of Education approved a new contract with the lunchroom workers union, which includes wage increases. This agreement aims to support school staff who play a direct role in students' daily school experience.

## Special Education

Recent reports indicate that parents of special education students in Chicago Public Schools (CPS) have raised concerns regarding their children's learning environments. Specifically, parents claim that some special education students are receiving instruction in hallways rather than designated classrooms.

This development highlights potential challenges within the district concerning the provision of appropriate and adequate learning spaces for students with disabilities. The claims bring attention to issues of resource allocation and the suitability of facilities for delivering specialized educational services in CPS.

## Budget & Finance

Recent reports highlight the significant financial implications surrounding the upcoming elected Chicago Public Schools (CPS) board. Campaign spending for board seats has now surpassed $9 million, indicating substantial interest and investment from various stakeholders in shaping the district's future governance and financial direction.

A key development anticipated with the transition to an elected board is a shift in how CPS secures its funding, particularly concerning property taxes. Historically, property tax increases for the district have often been a more predictable outcome. However, under the new elected board, these increases are expected to face greater scrutiny and will no longer be a "given," suggesting a potential change in how financial decisions are made and debated within the district.

## Board of Education & Governance

Recent coverage of Chicago's Board of Education and governance primarily focuses on the intensifying campaigns for the upcoming 2026 elected school board. A significant development is the substantial financial investment in these elections, with overall spending surpassing $9 million. Reports indicate that groups with considerable financial backing are outspending the Chicago Teachers Union by a notable margin, leading to discussions about the influence of these donors on the races.

The citywide race for School Board President is a key area of focus, with candidates Victor Henderson, Jessica Biggs, and Hilario Dominguez participating in multiple forums and debates. These discussions have addressed critical issues such as school budgets, potential school closings, and strategies to improve student achievement. A specific development involved candidate Hilario Dominguez, as the Chicago Public Schools Office of Inspector General closed an investigation into an allegation of sexual misconduct, stating there was insufficient evidence for an actionable finding.
